In [[conformal geometry]], the '''ambient construction''' refers to a construction of [[Charles Fefferman]] and [[C. Robin Graham|Robin Graham]]<ref>Fefferman, C. and Graham, R. "Conformal invariants", in ''Élie Cartan et les Mathématiques d'Aujourdui'', Asterisque (1985), 95-116.</ref> for which a [[conformal manifold]] of dimension ''n'' is realized (''ambiently'') as the boundary of a certain [[hyperbolic manifold|Poincaré manifold]], or alternatively as the [[celestial sphere]] of a certain [[pseudo-Riemannian]] manifold.

The ambient construction is canonical in the sense that it is performed only using the [[conformal class]] of the metric: it is conformally invariant.  However, the construction only works [[asymptotic]]ally, up to a certain [[order of approximation]].  There is, in general, an [[Obstruction theory|obstruction]] to continuing this extension past the critical order.  The obstruction itself is of tensorial character, and is known as the (conformal) '''obstruction tensor'''.  It is, along with the [[Weyl tensor]], one of the two primitive invariants in conformal differential geometry.

Aside from the obstruction tensor, the ambient construction can be used to define a class of conformally invariant [[differential operator]]s known as the [[GJMS operator]]s.<ref>Graham, R., Jenne, R., Mason, L.J., and Sparling, G.A.J. "Conformally invariant powers of the Laplacian I: Existence", ''Jour. Lond. Math. Soc'', '''46''' (1992), 557-565.</ref>

A related construction is the [[tractor bundle]].

==Overview==
The model flat geometry for the ambient construction is the future [[null cone]] in [[Minkowski space]], with the origin deleted.  The celestial sphere at infinity is the conformal manifold ''M'', and the null rays in the cone determine a [[line bundle]] over ''M''.  Moreover, the null cone carries a metric which degenerates in the direction of the generators of the cone.

The ambient construction in this flat model space then asks: if one is provided with such a line bundle, along with its degenerate metric, to what extent is it possible to ''extend'' the metric off the null cone in a canonical way, thus recovering the ambient Minkowski space?  In formal terms, the degenerate metric supplies a [[Dirichlet boundary condition]] for the extension problem and, as it happens, the natural condition is for the extended metric to be [[Ricci flat]] (because of the normalization of the [[normal conformal connection]].)

The ambient construction generalizes this to the case when ''M'' is conformally curved, first by constructing a natural null line bundle ''N'' with a degenerate metric, and then solving the associated Dirichlet problem on ''N'' &times; (-1,1).

==Details==
This section provides an overview of the construction, first of the null line bundle, and then of its ambient extension.

===The null line bundle===
Suppose that ''M'' is a conformal manifold, and that [''g''] denotes the conformal metric defined on ''M''.  Let &pi; : ''N'' &rarr; ''M'' denote the tautological subbundle of T<sup>*</sup>''M'' &otimes; T<sup>*</sup>''M'' defined by all representatives of the conformal metric.  In terms of a fixed background metric ''g''<sub>0</sub>, ''N'' consists of all positive multiples &omega;<sup>2</sup>''g''<sub>0</sub> of the metric.  There is a natural action of '''R'''<sup>+</sup> on ''N'', given by
:<math>\delta_\omega g = \omega^2 g</math>

Moreover, the [[total space]] of ''N'' carries a tautological degenerate metric, for if ''p'' is a point of the fibre of &pi; : ''N'' &rarr; ''M'' corresponding to the conformal representative ''g''<sub>p</sub>, then let
:<math>h_p(X_p,Y_p) = g_p(\pi_*X,\pi_*Y).</math>
This metric degenerates along the vertical directions.  Furthermore, it is homogeneous of degree 2 under the '''R'''<sup>+</sup> action on ''N'':
:<math>\delta^*_\omega h = \omega^2 h</math>

Let ''X'' be the vertical vector field generating the scaling action.  Then the following properties are immediate:
:''h''(''X'',-) = 0
:'''L'''<sub>X</sub>h = 2''h'', where '''L'''<sub>X</sub> is the [[Lie derivative]] along the vector field ''X''.

===The ambient space===
Let ''N''<sup>~</sup> = ''N'' &times; (-1,1), with the natural inclusion ''i'' : ''N'' &rarr; ''N''<sup>~</sup>.  The dilations &delta;<sub>&omega;</sub> extend naturally to ''N''<sup>~</sup>, and hence so does the generator ''X'' of dilation.

An '''ambient metric''' on ''N''<sup>~</sup> is a Lorentzian metric ''h''<sup>~</sup> such that
* The metric is ''homogeneous'': &delta;<sub>&omega;</sub><sup>*</sup> ''h''<sup>~</sup> = &omega;<sup>2</sup> ''h''<sup>~</sup>
* The metric is an ''ambient extension'':  ''i''<sup>*</sup> ''h''<sup>~</sup> = ''h'', where ''i''<sup>*</sup> is the [[pullback (differential geometry)|pullback]] along the natural inclusion.
* The metric is ''[[Ricci flat]]'': Ric(''h''<sup>~</sup>) = 0.

Suppose that a fixed representative of the conformal metric ''g'' and a local coordinate system ''x'' = (''x''<sup>i</sup>) are chosen on ''M''.  These induce coordinates on ''N'' by identifying a point in the fibre of ''N'' with (''x'',''t''<sup>2</sup>''g''(''x'')) where ''t'' > 0 is the fibre coordinate.  (In these coordinates, ''X'' = ''t'' ∂<sub>''t''</sub>.)  Finally, if &rho; is a defining function of ''N'' in ''N''<sup>~</sup> which is homogeneous of degree 0 under dilations, then (''x'',''t'',&rho;) are coordinates of ''N''<sup>~</sup>.  Furthermore, any extension metric which is homogeneous of degree 2 can be written in these coordinates in the form:
:<math>h^\sim = t^2 g_{ij}(x,\rho)dx^idx^j+2\rho dt^2+2tdtd\rho,\, </math>
where the ''g''<sub>ij</sub> are ''n''<sup>2</sup> functions with ''g''(''x'',0) = ''g''(''x''), the given conformal representative.

After some calculation<!--C.F. tells me this was published recently by Graham and Hirachi.  Find the citation!--> one shows that the Ricci flatness is equivalent to the following differential equation, where the prime is differentiation with respect to &rho;:
:<math>\rho g_{ij}''-\rho g^{kl}g_{ik}'g_{jl}+\tfrac12\rho g^{kl}g_{kl}'g_{ij}'+\frac{2-n}{2}g_{ij}'-\tfrac12 g^{kl}g_{kl}'g_{ij}+\mathrm{Ric}(g)_{ij}=0.</math>
One may then formally solve this equation as a power series in &rho; to obtain the asymptotic development of the ambient metric off the null cone.  For example, substituting &rho; = 0 and solving gives
:''g''<sub>ij</sub><sup>&prime;</sup>(''x'',0) = 2''P''<sub>ij</sub>
where ''P'' is the [[Schouten tensor]].  Next, differentiating again and substituting the known value of ''g''<sub>ij</sub><sup>&prime;</sup>(''x'',0) into the equation, the second derivative can be found to be a multiple of the [[Bach tensor]].  And so forth.
